attributes.title: Our Taste Test: what makes an app screen feel right?
attributes.brief: Learn what this person looks for in the look and feel of everyday app screens (dashboards, lists, forms, settings), so we can tune how our AI designs Boxel cards. The study can show 18 real app screens from our Matrix taste test (order fulfilment, contracts, club membership, service desk, academy), mixing real products, designers' concepts and our AI's own concepts, without saying which is which. We want their honest preferences, not what they think a designer would say: how dense or airy they like a screen, playful or serious, what they notice first, what makes a screen feel trustworthy or cheap, and the trade-offs they'd make (looks vs speed, familiar vs fresh). The findings go to our design team and are pooled across people; participants don't get a personal result.
attributes.aims:
How dense or airy they like a screen
Playful or serious: which tone they prefer for tools they use daily
What they notice first on a new screen
What makes a screen feel trustworthy, and what makes it feel cheap
The trade-offs they'd make: looks vs speed, familiar vs fresh
attributes.mustAsk: What's one app whose look you love, and what about it?

We're curious about what you like in app screen designs.", "reveal": "none", "rapport": "balanced", "adapt": true, "warmup": 1, "showNotes": false, "showAims": false, "minutes": 20, "offerMore": true, "tools": ["choice", "likert", "duels", "picture", "video"], "measures": [{"aim": "How dense or airy they like a screen", "kind": "pair", "poles": ["dense", "airy"]}, {"aim": "Playful or serious: which tone they prefer for tools they use daily", "kind": "pair", "poles": ["playful", "serious"]}, {"aim": "What they notice first on a new screen", "kind": "open"}, {"aim": "What makes a screen feel trustworthy, and what makes it feel cheap", "kind": "open"}, {"aim": "The trade-offs they'd make: looks vs speed, familiar vs fresh", "kind": "open"}], "rationale": "The 'none' reveal and 'balanced' rapport prevent biasing future answers or making participants feel they need to give a 'correct' design opinion. Hiding aims ensures honest, uninfluenced preferences. A moderate length and 'offerMore' respects participant time while allowing for deeper exploration if they're engaged. The chosen tools allow for both structured preference gathering and open-ended insights into their design tastes."}
